chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awadd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I saw him, when he raised his head from the second prostration of the first rak'ah, sitting until he was at ease, then he would stand up.

key_terms.يَطْمَئِنَّ: to be at ease / stable (ritual stability)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting after the second prostration of the first rak'ah in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s or Imam’s adherence to *tuma'ninah* (tranquil stability) in prayer, a key criterion for the validity of movements in Shia jurisprudence. By pausing after the second prostration of the first rak'ah, the Imam demonstrates the Sunnah of deliberate, composed transitions, distinguishing ritual perfection from mere mechanical completion. This practice underscores the spiritual dimension of Salah, where physical stillness facilitates mental presence (khushu').
